title: Accident investigation and 'Four No Pass' principle
summary: We enforce a root cause-focused investigation completed within 7 working days, using the 5-Why method and the 'Four No Pass' closure rule.

content.overview: All incidents undergo mandatory investigation following the 'Four No Pass' principle: no closure until the direct and root causes are identified, responsible persons are handled, corrective measures are implemented, and all relevant personnel are re-educated. Investigations are documented within 7 working days.
content.details: We require both direct cause analysis and a 5-Why root cause analysis to prevent superficial fixes. The 7-day deadline ensures timely learning and corrective action, balancing thoroughness with urgency. The 'Four No Pass' principle creates a systematic loop: investigation → accountability → correction → awareness, so that similar events are prevented through organizational learning, not just punishment. Choosing the 5-Why method over more complex techniques (like TapRooT) keeps the investigation simple and participative at site level, though for major events a formal root cause analysis team may augment.
content.examples: After a scaffolding collapse, 5-Why: Why did scaffold fall? Ledger missing pin. Why pin missing? Not installed during erection. Why not installed? Crew skipped after lunch. Why skipped? No post-break pre-use inspection. Why no inspection? Superintendent not enforcing checklist. Corrective actions: enforce checklist sign-off, retrain crew, add post-break inspection to JSA. Investigation report issued within 5 working days.
content.caveats: 5-Why can stop too early if not facilitated by an experienced person; must be paired with evidence collection. The 7-day deadline may be challenging for complex incidents; extensions should be justified. Emphasis on education over blame can be misinterpreted as leniency if accountability is not clearly addressed.
